t: You're standing at Lincoln's Inn Fields, in Holborn, the largest public square in London. It was laid out in the 1630s on the initiative of the builder William Newton, and Inigo Jones is said to have drawn the original plan. Plenty of notable people have lived or died around the square. William Blackstone, whose Commentaries on the Laws of England became the best-known account of English common law, lived here. The Duke of Newcastle, who served as Prime Minister, died here, as did George Calvert, the first Baron Baltimore, and the naval officer Murray Maxwell.
